messages.subject: Error trying to combine three stacks
parts:
I'm trying to predict from a model using misaligned covariates. Xavier Barber has been helping me based on his study - stk.x is my primary data, stk.y is a misaligned point array with covariate data, and stk.pred is a grid where I'd like to make predictions. I am getting an error, though, when I try to combine them into a single stack.

> A.x <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = loc_x)
> A.y <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = loc_y)
> A.pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = p.coords)
> 
> 
> stk.x <- inla.stack(tag='est.x',
+                     data=list(y=cbind(data$result, NA)),
+                     A=list(A.x, 1),
+                     effects=list(xi.field=1:spde$n.spde,
+                                  id=data$id))
> 
> 
> stk.y <- inla.stack(data=list(y=cbind(NA, cmv$result)),
+                     A = list(A.y, 1),
+                     tag ='est.y',
+                     effects=list(list(u.field=1:spde$n.spde, 
+                                       x.field=1:spde$n.spde),
+                                  list(intercept = rep(1, length(cmv$result)))))
> 
> 
> stk.pred <- inla.stack(tag='prediction',
+                        data=list(y=NA),
+                        A=list(A.pred, 1),
+                        effects=list(s=1:spde$n.spde,
+                                     list(id=grid$id)))
> 
> stk <- inla.stack(data=list(stk.x, stk.y, stk.pred))
Error in (function (data, A, effects, tag = "", compress = TRUE, remove.unused = TRUE)  : 
  argument "A" is missing, with no default

> stk <- inla.stack(stk.x, stk.y, stk.pred)
Error in (function (...)  : Name mismatch.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error trying to combine three stacks
parts:
Of your two stack join attempts at the end, the first is invalid.
The second one is correct.
The error is that your reduction stack needs to also have the data "y" as a two column matrix, y = cbind(NA, NA).

The error message from R isn't very helpful; I can probably catch the error earlier and give a more specific message instead.
